title: It's a pause, not a verdict

beats.vo: If your body switches off for a minute, it's not over.
beats.visual_intent: Light switch on a dark wall, close-up.

beats.vo: Nerves can make your body's response come and go, especially the first time with someone new. That's your body reacting to pressure, not failing you.
beats.visual_intent: Candle flame flickering in the dark, close-up.

beats.vo: The problem starts when you panic about it, because panicking keeps you stuck in your head and makes it harder to settle back into the moment.
beats.visual_intent: Rough sea waves at dusk, dark tones, no people.

beats.vo: Don't stop and apologize. Slow down, stay close, and keep your attention on her.
beats.visual_intent: Calm lake at dusk, still water, no people.

beats.vo: Kiss her, talk to her, take your time. Nobody's keeping score.
beats.visual_intent: Warm string lights softly out of focus, dark room.

beats.vo: Treat it like a pause, not a verdict. Most guys never hear that this happens, so the first time it does, it feels like a disaster. It isn't.
beats.visual_intent: Sunrise through a window, soft warm light, no people.
